messages:
carla: heads-up: seeing ~6-12% of traces from payments-service missing the span for the batching shard. spike started ~00:10 UTC, aligns with a flurry of exporter backoffs.
ben: do you have a sample trace id? can we see exporter logs + queue metrics?
carla: sample trace: 0af7651916cd43dd8448eb211c80319c
carla: short logs from collector around the time: ```2025-06-12T00:10:13Z collector exporter=https://ingest.redwood/api/v1/spans level=warn msg="exporter backoff: 429 received" retry_after=2s queue_len=510 queue_capacity=512 dropped=3```
carla: also a few lines later: ```exporter worker=3 msg="queue eviction: oldest batch evicted" evicted_spans=128 reason=queue_full```
alice: eviction of whole batches would explain missing intermediate spans for long traces. if a batch contains parent+children and a batch is evicted, the trace looks truncated.
ben: timeline from metrics: exporter_retries surged, queue_size hit capacity, then queue_evictions increased. what's odd: dropped spans count is small vs evicted_spans. evicted means we lose earlier batches.
sre-oncall: console graph: trace-reassembly-latency climbs before the dropoff. retention TTL for stream is 1h, but this is immediate loss in-flight, not retention expiration.
carla: hypothesis: spike in downstream 429s triggered backoff loop. collector uses constant backoff + strict queue eviction (FIFO batch evict) which disproportionately loses earlier spans for multi-batch traces.
ben: can we change behavior to partial_flush or split-batches-by-trace-id? config snippet we tested locally: ```exporters: otlp/https: endpoint: https://ingest.redwood/api/v1/spans timeout: 10s retry: max_interval: 30s initial_interval: 0.5s backoff: exponential queue: enabled: true max_size: 4096 eviction_policy: discard_oldest_batch partial_flush: true```
alice: partial_flush:true looks promising — will flush available spans for a trace instead of holding until full batch. also eviction_policy: discard_oldest_batch is the problem; prefer discard_oldest_span or backpressure block with more aggressive backoff jitter so we don't fill queue.
carla: I rolled a quick config to increase queue max_size to 2048 and enabled partial_flush on a canary collector at us-west. deploy-bot: deploy started for collector-canary (rev 2025.06.12-17)
deploy-bot: canary deploy complete — collector-canary healthy
carla: after canary, observed evicted_spans dropped to 0 and missing-span rate fell to ~0.5% within 90s.
ben: good signal. need a robust fix: options: 1) change eviction policy to per-span discard, 2) enable partial_flush by default + tune batch size, 3) implement exponential jitter backoff to avoid synchronized retries.
alice: also add a dashboard alert: "evicted_batches > 0" + link to traces with long trace length. and add a one-off runbook for when exporter 429 spikes occur: increase queue, enable partial_flush, check downstream throttling.
sre-oncall: filing incident ticket and tagging infra-cost for longer queue sizes.
ben: next actions: I'll open a PR to change eviction_policy and default partial_flush, include a migration test for multi-batch traces. carla: please attach sample traces and the logs to the PR. alice: I'll add dashboard panels and an alert rule.
carla: thanks — leaving collector-canary up for 2h then we'll roll to prod if no regressions. :thumbsup:
ben: assign me for PR review. :eyes:
sre-oncall: incident ticket created: INC-2025-1749 (linked in the thread).
carla: marking as monitored. will update if anything else crops up.
ben: quick note for the console UX team — the traces view should highlight traces that span across multiple batches and flag when batch drop occurs so customers can correlate with eviction metrics.
alice: noted, I'll follow up in product channel with a mock for the dashboard flag.
carla: thanks everyone.
